message:
Avoid materializing `descendants` when resolving an STI subclass

`find_sti_class` guarded the resolved class with
`descendants.include?(subclass)`. `descendants` is not memoized: every call
walks `Class#subclasses` recursively and allocates two arrays per node, and
the result is then scanned linearly. This runs once per record for every
STI model that is instantiated, from `find`, `instantiate` and
`subclass_from_attributes` alike.

`subclass <= self` answers the same question. For classes it is true exactly
when `self` is among `subclass.ancestors`, which is what a transitive walk of
`Class#subclasses` from `self` computes, and `sti_class_for` only ever
returns a class that is currently bound to a constant, so the reloading
filter that `descendants` applies cannot change the answer. It walks the
ancestor chain instead and allocates nothing.

On a base class with 46 subclasses one lookup went from 14.4 µs and 141
allocations to 0.02 µs and none; instantiating 45 such records per request
dropped allocations for the request by about half.
